children: Aragon has launched Confidential Voting, an Aragon OSx plugin built on the Zama Protocol. Individual votes remain encrypted while they are counted, with only the final tally revealed. The plugin also supports programmable confidentiality rules, allowing organizations to configure privacy settings for compliance requirements. The release moves encrypted on-chain governance from concept to a working product flow.

For ZAMA and ANT holders, the launch provides a concrete fully homomorphic encryption adoption datapoint rather than a roadmap promise. A live governance product gives the Zama Protocol a measurable usage channel, since every Confidential Voting deployment routes vote processing through its encryption stack. That could support protocol-usage narratives for both tokens, though actual adoption by DAOs will determine how much weight the datapoint carries.
Another major onchain use case becomes confidential: governance.
